newsitem.title: USA: Steep growth goal for Columbia home-care - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Steep growth goal for Columbia home-care - WSJ.

text.p: Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp laid out aggressive growth targets for its home-care division in an internal company memo, the Wall Street Journal said in Friday's electronic edition.

Last year, the company set a target of guiding as many as 85 percent of patients discharged from its hospitals and going to home health care into Columbia-owned health care agencies, the paper said, citing people who saw the memo.
"I raised Cain about that," Randy Boston, a former executive at the Columbia Homecare Group unit who saw the memo, was quoted as saying. "I felt it would jeopardize the patient's right to choose."
According to the newspaper, Boston said he was asked to resign last autumn for being "nonsupportive."
The company was not immediately available to comment.

Spokeswoman Eve Hutcherson was quoted in the paper as saying "there was a document that had that number in it. I don't know if it was the memo (those people) are talking about." Hutcherson said the document also said Columbia was "obligated to protect patient choice."
